text:
samir: Hey all — Sparrowhawk POC hit us in the middle of the demo. Slow TTFT (1.0-1.5s) on small prompts and occasional 429s after a few minutes. Can ops/engineers swarm? :eyes:
elaine: Oof. Customer on Dedicated trial or hosted? Pricing/commit questions incoming too.
samir: Hosted, sandbox cluster in us-west-2. They were ramping traffic with a demo script (~10 rps burst). No dedicated yet.
ryan: On it — can you paste the request headers and the example payload? Also need the endpoint + model variant.
samir: Example curl we used:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"Summarize: This is a test\n","max_tokens":64,"prefill":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=redwood-13b-v2
```
Response time for first token ~1.2s, then steady stream. After ~3m demo we started seeing 429s: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":15}`.
maria: Two quick askables: 1) Are they using prefill/prefill_policy override? 2) Any VPC egress / NAT gateway errors in their cloud logs?
samir: They enabled prefill=true in the script. No VPC in the test account (hosted). No NAT issues reported.
ryan: Ok — likely two concurrent things: (A) batching window conflicts causing early-token latency, and (B) transient capacity contention hitting per-tenant rate limits leading to 429s.
elaine: Pricing question from Sparrowhawk: if we recommend increasing reserved concurrency / dedicated lanes for the demo, what's the min commit and cost delta? Sales will handle but want rough numbers to suggest during call.
ryan: Quick technical triage steps I recommend now:
1) Turn off prefill (prefill=false) for a quick A/B to see TTFT impact.
2) Set batch_window_ms to 8 (was default 20) to reduce artificial batching delay for small prompts.
3) Temporarily bump tenant token rate_limit to 30rps for them (ops to confirm) to avoid 429 while demo.
4) Enable KV prefix caching on the route if they have repeated prefixes.
5) If 429s persist, route their traffic to a spare dedicated pool (if available).

maria: Ops notes: I can bump rate_limit for their tenant in the console (will leave an audit log). Also watching pod queue_depth and shard_queue latencies. Deploy-bot: trigger snapshot of serving metrics now.
deploy-bot: Snapshot captured: serving/pool=us-west-2-sandbox, timestamp=3214567902. Metrics: avg_ttft=1.18s, p95_ttft=1.34s, queue_depth=48, inflight_batches=6, kv_cache_hit=12%. Top error=429: capacity_exceeded.
ryan: KV cache hit 12% is low — suggests they're not benefiting from prefix reuse. If the demo has repeated system prompts, we should enable prefix/kvcache prefill. Also queue_depth=48 is high for a small burst — look at burst smoothing.
samir: Quick A/B: I disabled prefill and reduced batch_window to 8ms locally. Re-run demo now.
samir: New numbers: avg_ttft=0.42s p95=0.55s. No 429s in the first 90s. Looks much better.
elaine: Great — so we can recommend prefill=false + lower batch window for interactive demos. For production, we should discuss KV prefill and dedicated lanes.
maria: Filed an ops ticket (OPS-4821) to temporarily raise tenant rps and monitor. Also added a routing rule to fallback to smaller model on stepdown when queue_depth>60 to avoid user-visible errors.
ryan: Follow-ups for eng/product: consider smarter auto-batch heuristics that detect interactive tiny prompts and shrink window automatically. I'll file a short PR proposal.
samir: Customer happy for now. They asked about pricing: what commitment to reserve a small dedicated pool for predictable latency?
elaine: I'll send a draft: suggest a minimal monthly commit equivalent to ~0.5k GPU-hours for a small steady demo lane — estimate attached in DM. Also mention ability to burst on demand (credits).
ryan: Note for the record — root cause in this run: prefill+large batch_window triggered batching tail latency; combined with tenant-level concurrency limits caused backpressure and 429s once queue filled. Workarounds: prefill toggle, lower batch_window, temporary rate bump, and dedicated pool.
samir: Thanks all. I'll follow up with the customer summary and include ops ticket + suggested commit. Closing swarm unless new errors pop up. :thumbsup:
